surveyDefinition.title: Video Streaming Subscriptions — consumer survey (Global)
surveyDefinition.studyPurpose: Identify which of 5 behavioural segments each respondent belongs to, based on viewing habits, subscription management, spend behaviour, and content motivations.

segments.name: High-Engagement Subscribers
segments.description: Heavy daily viewers who subscribe to multiple services, are willing to pay for premium ad-free experiences, and are driven by exclusive content and immediate access to new releases. They rarely cancel and see streaming as their primary entertainment.

segments.name: Price-Sensitive Subscribers
segments.description: Cost-conscious subscribers who frequently cancel and re-subscribe based on content drops and promotions. They actively compare plans, use ad-supported tiers to save money, and are quick to churn when prices rise.

segments.name: Household Co-Viewers
segments.description: Subscribers who manage streaming as a shared family resource, prioritizing multiple profiles, parental controls, and content that appeals to different ages. They value simultaneous streams and family-friendly libraries over individual preferences.

segments.name: Niche Content Customers
segments.description: Viewers with strong genre or language preferences who subscribe to specialized services to access content unavailable on mainstream platforms. They are willing to pay for niche libraries but are frustrated by fragmentation and poor subtitles.

segments.name: Occasional Lapsed Users
segments.description: Low-frequency viewers who subscribe for a single title or a short period, then cancel and stay unsubscribed for months. They are the least loyal, most price-sensitive, and often rely on free or ad-supported options between subscriptions.

surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A segmentation study of Video Streaming Subscriptions buyers worldwide. It asks how people use Video Streaming Subscriptions, how they choose it, and what would make them switch — then sorts respondents into the behavioural groups defined below. Questions stay at category level: no named brands, and nothing about adjacent categories. This global view is not a separate fieldwork exercise: it selects the strongest questions from the regional surveys and blends their percentages using population-style regional weights.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults worldwide who buy or use Video Streaming Subscriptions for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Currently holds an active subscription to at least one video streaming service (e.g., Netflix, Disney+, Hulu, Amazon Prime Video, HBO Max, etc.); Personally pays for the subscription (not solely through a bundled telecom or employer plan); Makes or significantly influences the household's streaming subscription decisions. Excluded: Individuals who only watch free ad-supported streaming (e.g., free tiers of Pluto TV, Tubi) and do not pay for any subscription; Businesses or institutions purchasing streaming for commercial use (e.g., bars, hotels); Cord-cutters who have never subscribed to a paid streaming service.
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Household consumers buy video streaming subscriptions for personal entertainment, pay the subscription fees themselves, and decide which services to subscribe to based on content preferences and price. Businesses may occasionally purchase for employee perks, but the dominant and defining purchase is by individual consumers.
respondentBehaviours: Streams video content regularly (multiple times per week)
Subscribes to one or more streaming services
Churns between services based on content libraries and pricing
Engages with original programming and exclusive content
Uses multiple devices (smart TV, phone, tablet, laptop) to watch
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income as behavioural questions — no finding in this survey is driven by them. They are asked once, at the end, in Profiling, and used only to cross-tabulate the behavioural results.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

sections.label: Streaming Consumption & Viewing Context
sections.covers: Establish how respondents use streaming in their daily lives — which services they hold, how viewing fits their week, who watches with them, and what role streaming plays.

sections.label: Subscription Acquisition & Management
sections.covers: Understand the triggers, discovery, and management of streaming subscriptions — including how they sign up, how they pay, and how they share accounts.

sections.label: Content & Service Requirements
sections.covers: Capture what respondents require from a streaming service — content library, features, ad tolerance, and value expectations — and the trade-offs they are willing to make.

sections.label: Satisfaction, Loyalty & Churn Risk
sections.covers: Measure overall satisfaction, identify friction points, and understand what would trigger cancellation or switching, plus future intent and interest in bundles.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's current streaming landscape — which services they hold, how they watch, and who in the household is involved. It then moves into the subscription lifecycle: what triggers a new sign-up, how they compare and manage services, and what they spend. Next, it probes the content and feature requirements that drive service choice, including ad tolerance and family features. Finally, it measures satisfaction, friction, and churn risk to understand loyalty and future behaviour. This arc separates the segments by their engagement level, price…

segmentModel.tie_break: The question 'sf5' (When a show you follow ends, what do you usually do with the subscription?) is the most direct behavioural self-report to distinguish between high_engagement_subscribers (keep it running) and price_sensitive_rotators (cancel and come back), as it captures the core churn behaviour that defines the two segments.
notes: Occasional lapsed users are identified by low usage, reliance on free/ads, and cancellation due to low usage or show ending.
Niche content fans are identified by specific content needs, foreign language, and subtitle frustrations.
Household co-viewers are identified by watching with family, shared decision-making, and family-friendly features.
High engagement subscribers are identified by heavy usage, multiple subscriptions, willingness to pay for premium features, and low churn.
Price sensitive rotators are identified by frequent switching, promotional offers, and cost-driven decisions.
segmentModel.excluded: Screening and Profiling questions are excluded from scoring: screeners carry no signal (everyone passed) and demographics are for cross-tabs, not segmentation.

fieldingNotes.recommendedSample: n=800-1,200 for stable segment-level sub-groups (roughly n>=250 per segment after weighting). At n=1,000 the margin of error on a whole-sample percentage is about ±3.1pp at 95% confidence; on a segment of n=200 it widens to about ±6.9pp, so segment-level differences under ~10pp should not be reported as real.
fieldingNotes.quotaControls: Apply quotas on the category-usage and frequency screeners so heavy users — who are more willing survey-takers — are not over-sampled.
scriptingNotes: Rotate the order of answer options on every non-ordinal question to remove primacy bias. Do NOT rotate ordinal scales (frequency bands, price bands, satisfaction) — their order carries meaning.
Anchor 'Other', 'None of these' and 'Prefer not to say' to the bottom of the list, exempt from rotation.
Every 'Other' option takes an open-text capture, coded back into the frame at analysis if any single verbatim exceeds 3%.
No routing or skip logic: every respondent sees every question, so the base is constant across the instrument.
Include one attention check in the middle third — a standard instructed-response item. Terminate on failure and replace.
Randomise the order of the two ranking/trade-off items between respondents so neither is systematically answered while fresher.
caveats: Percentages in this document are simulated from a persona-weighted panel, not fielded with real respondents. Replace with primary data after fielding.
Ranking items are shown as a lighter-weight ranking exercise; run them as MaxDiff if you need more precision on driver importance.
Profiling questions are for cross-tabs only and are excluded from the segmentation scoring model.
